item.title: Hamilton says he remains all-in on Formula One at 41
item.description: Lewis Hamilton said he could still be racing when Formula One returns to Africa in the 2030s, but would retire if his reactions or pace decline. The seven-time champion is using the final five races to help Ferrari prepare its 2027 car.

item.title: Dream force a winner-take-all Game 7 in the WNBA Finals
item.description: Atlanta beat Golden State 80-69 in Game 6, sending the WNBA Finals to its first winner-take-all Game 7. Allisha Gray scored 23 and Rhyne Howard 21 as the Dream answered the controversy over an early-afternoon tip with a decisive home win.

item.title: Bears acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons
item.description: Chicago is sending Tennessee first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 plus a 2027 fourth-rounder for Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, pending a physical. The four-time Pro Bowler signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension this summer.

item.title: Brewers capture their first World Series championship
item.description: Milwaukee ended a 57-season wait by beating Tampa Bay 4-1 in Game 5. Rookie Cooper Pratt drove in two runs, Jacob Misiorowski worked 5 2/3 scoreless innings and William Contreras earned World Series MVP honors.

item.title: Jokic becomes the second NBA player with 200 triple-doubles
item.description: Nikola Jokic joined Russell Westbrook as the only NBA players to reach 200 career triple-doubles, collecting 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in Denver's 104-91 victory over New Orleans.

item.title: MLS details its 2027 sprint season before shifting the calendar
item.description: Inter Miami and Cincinnati will open a 14-game bridge season on February 19 as MLS moves toward an autumn-to-spring calendar. The sprint concludes with Decision Day on May 8 and playoffs later that month.

item.title: Rays walk off the Brewers in the 12th to extend the World Series
item.description: Ben Williamson's bases-loaded single completed a two-run rally in the bottom of the 12th as Tampa Bay beat Milwaukee 4-3. The Rays avoided a sweep and forced Game 5, though the Brewers still lead the series 3-1.

item.title: Tatum's overtime buzzer-beater lifts the Celtics over the Nets
item.description: Jayson Tatum capped an overtime thriller with a winning shot at the horn, leading Boston past Brooklyn. The dramatic finish headlined Tuesday night's NBA action.

item.title: Harry Kane becomes the first English Ballon d'Or winner since 2001
item.description: Kane won football's top individual prize after scoring 61 goals for Bayern Munich and leading England to a World Cup semifinal. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's award for a third time.

item.title: Brewers move one win from first World Series title after 10-1 rout
item.description: Jackson Chourio went 4-for-5 and capped an eight-run fifth inning as Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 10-1 in Game 3. Robert Gasser faced the minimum through six innings, and the Brewers moved within one victory of their first championship.

item.title: Cowboys pull away from Eagles as Prescott throws three touchdowns
item.description: Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes and Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards in Dallas’s 38-21 victory at Philadelphia. The Eagles briefly led in the third quarter before allowing 18 unanswered points and losing their fifth straight.

item.title: Cavaliers erase 15-point deficit and hand Timberwolves first loss
item.description: Donovan Mitchell’s late jumper helped Cleveland beat previously unbeaten Minnesota 127-125 in overtime despite Anthony Edwards scoring 47. Golden State also earned its first win behind Stephen Curry’s perfect shooting night and 31 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

item.title: Falcons hand the 49ers their first loss in a day of NFL upsets
item.description: Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes and Atlanta forced four turnovers in a 29-20 win over previously unbeaten San Francisco. Seattle also dealt Kansas City its first loss, while Pittsburgh won the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris.

item.title: Antonelli wins U.S. Grand Prix and closes on youngest F1 title
item.description: Kimi Antonelli led from pole and won by more than 13 seconds for his ninth victory of the season. The Mercedes driver needs only two points in Mexico to clinch the championship and become Formula One’s youngest title winner.

item.title: Mbappé brace wins El Clásico and ends Barcelona’s perfect start
item.description: Kylian Mbappé scored twice, including a late winner, as Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 at Camp Nou. Barcelona’s first league defeat of the season cut its lead over Madrid to three points.
